transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Miguel Sanchez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO), Ben Ortiz (Head of Infra), Dr. Samir Patel (Security), Lina Ho (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed on-prem air-gapped requirements, constraints on updating images, GPU inventory, and compliance controls. Agreed to follow up with security docs and SE-run benchmark plan.

Topics: on-prem private deployment, air-gapped update workflow, hardware compatibility, KMS/HSM, audit logs, maintenance windows, pilot scope and timeline.

Transcript:
00:00 Miguel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Miguel Sanchez from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Aisha: Doing good, thanks. Appreciate you carving the time.
00:10 Ben: Yep, afternoon.
00:12 Miguel: Great — goal today is to understand your constraints for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment and outline what a pilot might look like. Priya will cover technical bits and I'll cover commercial and next steps. Sound good?
00:24 Aisha: Yep, that's perfect. I'll hand it over to Ben to walk through infra.
00:28 Ben: Sure. Quick context: CentraCorp is a regulated healthcare data provider, PHI heavy. We cannot have any egress to the public internet from the inference nodes. Our standard pattern is an air-gapped cluster in our on-prem DCs; updates happen via secure media and change-control windows.
00:45 Priya: Got it. When you say air-gapped, is there any kind of controlled outbound like a jump host that pulls updates into the environment? Or is it literally zero egress?
00:55 Ben: We have a bastion that can be used for pull-only, but it itself is managed by our security team and only during scheduled windows. For third-party vendors we usually ship artifacts on signed USBs or via an internal package repo that is populated from a guarded jump host.
01:08 Priya: Okay, that helps. On the Redwood side, our Private deployment can run in a fully isolated VPC or on-prem. For air-gap we provide an offline bundle — container images and model artifacts — plus a documented install flow. The updates can be delivered as signed archives and validated locally.
01:22 Ben: How do you handle model weights updates? Our security team won't allow inbound pulls to model registries.
01:28 Priya: Models and weights are included in the offline bundle. For larger models we can provide shard manifests and delta updates. We also support checksum verification and signing so your team can validate integrity. In the installer we support a flag for offline mode which disables any telemetry and external downloads.
01:44 Dr. Samir: Quick Q — what about KMS/HSM integration? We can't hand any plaintext keys to a vendor.
01:50 Priya: We support customer-managed KMS; our Private control plane can be configured to use your HSM or cloud KMS via local gateway. For fully air-gapped setups we typically integrate with an on-prem HSM (Luna, AWS CloudHSM in VPC mode if allowed) and keep private keys within your boundary.
02:05 Aisha: Do you require root on the inference hosts? Our policy restricts vendor access to root.
02:11 Ben: Yeah, we limit sudo.
02:13 Priya: You do not need to give us root. The operator bundle runs as a Kubernetes operator or systemd service and can be managed by your engineers. For troubleshooting we usually provide runbooks and logs; if deeper access is required we can do a remote session under your supervision or accept logs and crash dumps via the secure channel.
02:28 Miguel: There's often a question on hardware. Ben, do you have GPUs in the target clusters?
02:33 Ben: We have a mix — some newer A100s in one DC, but the site we want to pilot on has older P40 / V100 class cards with constrained memory — about 16GB. We also are limited on kernel updates; we can't upgrade drivers without a maintenance window booked weeks in advance.
02:50 Priya: That's useful to know. Our runtime supports quantized models and can run on 16GB cards with reduced batch sizes and sequence length. Performance will be impacted; we'll include expected latency ranges. We also have a 'low memory profile' that reduces KV cache shine and uses CPU offload for certain ops.
03:07 Miguel: Does that fit into your performance SLOs? What are your latency goals?
03:11 Aisha: For the first phase we need 95th percentile under 600ms for typical chat prompts (avg 150 tokens). It's okay if the POC shows degraded throughput as long as we can demonstrate a consistent profile and fallbacks.
03:25 Priya: 600ms 95p on a V100 with 16GB for 150 tokens is aggressive but may be achievable with model distillation/quantization and batching thresholds. We'll put this as a hypothesis for the benchmark. For production we might recommend either Dedicated capacity in our private tenant or upgrading GPUs.
03:41 Ben: What's the difference between Redwood Dedicated and the Private on-prem offering? Sometimes in our last notes we saw 'Redford' — can't remember.
03:47 Miguel: (laughs) That's a common transcription. Quick summary: Hosted Redwood API is our cloud service. Redwood Dedicated is reserved, single-tenant capacity managed by Redwood in our infra (still requires network access). Private is the customer-managed deployment that runs inside your network or on-prem. For air-gap you want Private.
04:03 Dr. Samir: About audit logs: we need immutability and a specific retention policy, plus export to our SIEM. Can your operator provide those logs?
04:12 Priya: Yes, we emit structured audit logs for every request, auth event, and administrative action. In air-gapped mode logs are written locally and can be forwarded to your SIEM via your log shipper. We support file-based append-only logs, and we can sign rotation files if you need tamper-evidence.
04:29 Aisha: How about evals and quality monitoring? We need regression alerts if a new model or quantization pass reduces accuracy for key prompts.
04:38 Priya: We offer an eval harness that can be run inside your environment. For offline setups we'll include the eval runner and a baseline prompt set. The Eval results are artifacts you keep; we also offer a small aggregator that runs locally and raises alerts based on thresholds you set.
04:53 Ben: Networking question — our infra team blocks outbound DNS by default. How will your operator resolve images or dependencies during install?
05:00 Priya: The offline installer is self-contained; images are loaded from tarballs via our installer. No DNS outbound required. If you want to use your internal registry we provide manifests to push images internally.
05:13 Lina: What about updates and CVEs? We have a strict SLA for patch windows and need signed patches.
05:18 Priya: We produce signed update bundles and a CVE bulletin with each release. For the POC we can commit to a specific patch cadence and tie upgrades to your change-control dates.
05:28 Miguel: On commercial side, typical POC length is 4-6 weeks; pricing varies based on hardware and whether Redwood supports managed services. For fully private, air-gapped installs, there's an enterprise license + support; we can share a draft SOW.
05:40 Aisha: Timeline-wise we are planning compliance review early October, so ideally start a POC mid-September.
05:46 Miguel: That aligns — we'll aim to have the security pack over to you by Thursday and schedule the SE deep dive next week. Priya, can you run through what you'll need for the benchmark?
05:55 Priya: Sure. For the benchmark we need: model family / expected size, sample prompt set (we can use sanitized prompts), access to their target hardware (exact GPU model, driver, CUDA version), and a small dataset for throughput/latency tests. For air-gap we'll produce an execution plan that you run locally; if we need to run ourselves it'll be via remote session with your Bastion during the window.
06:18 Ben: We can provide sanitized prompts. For hardware, I'll collate the exact driver versions.
06:22 Priya: Great. Also want to call out fallback policies — in your policies you may want to fallback to smaller model or to on-device caching if a node goes down; our router supports policy-based routing but in fully private mode it's configured by your operators.
06:36 Aisha: One last for now — licensing for model weights. If we use an open model, do we need to license separately?
06:42 Priya: Typically open models are covered by their upstream licenses; Redwood provides redistribution for the offline bundle under our vendor terms. For any proprietary/redwood-verified models we'd include license terms in the SOW. We'll call that out explicitly.
06:56 Dr. Samir: Also need an explicit articulation of data flow for audits — where tokens are cached, how long, and who can access them.
07:04 Priya: We set token retention policy; you can configure zero retention for sensitive endpoints, and KV cache is ephemeral; persistent caches are optional and encrypted at rest using your KMS. We'll document exact flow.
07:17 Miguel: Okay, timing — we'll send the security docs (SOC2/ISO artifacts), sample SOW, and proposed POC scope. Next step is Priya scheduling the deep dive with Ben/Lina for network and hardware walkthrough.
07:29 Aisha: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
07:31 Miguel: Thanks folks. We'll follow up with links: security pack (link) and draft SOW.

Notes / references mentioned:
- Security pack (SOC2, ISO artifacts), KMS integration notes — to be shared (link placeholder).
- Offline installer and signed bundle process — described by Priya.
- Benchmark plan to be executed in-airgap or via bastion session.

End of transcript.

Caveats: Transcription may have mis-typed product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicated vs "Redford"), and some timestamps are approximate.
